properties.areaDesc: Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands; Ventura County Beaches; Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 5 at 2:47PM PDT until October 7 at 6:00AM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents
and breaking waves due to elevated surf expected. For the
Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding and elevated surf
expected.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands, Ventura County
Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, from Tuesday afternoon
through late Tuesday night. For the Coastal Flood Advisory,
from 6 AM Wednesday to 11 PM PDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely.
Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an
increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can wash people off
beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats nearshore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Coastal flooding impacts will be greatest
for Long Beach, Catalina Island, Zuma Beach and Malibu.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 5 at 4:30PM EDT until October 5 at 7:30PM EDT by NWS Jacksonville FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southern Clay County in northeastern Florida...
Northwestern Putnam County in northeastern Florida...
East Central Alachua County in northern Florida...
Southeastern Bradford County in northern Florida...

* WHEN...Until 730 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 430 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have
fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Palatka, Keystone Heights, Melrose, George's Lake, Florahome,
Lake Geneva, Melrose Landing, Bardin, Orange Heights and Putnam
Hall.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.description:
* WHAT...North winds 15 to 25 kt with gusts up to 30 kt and steep
seas 6 to 9 ft.

* WHERE...All areas. The strongest winds and highest seas are
expected south of Port Orford.

* WHEN..From 11 PM Sunday to 11 PM PDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds and/or steep seas could capsize or
damage smaller vessels.

* View the hazard area in detail at https://go.usa.gov/x6hks
properties.instruction:
Inexperienced mariners and those operating smaller vessels should
remain in port and avoid the area of hazardous conditions.

properties.headline: Hazardous Seas Warning issued October 5 at 1:21PM PDT until October 7 at 5:00PM PDT by NWS Medford OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...North winds 20 to 30 kt with gusts up to 35 kt and steep
to very steep and hazardous seas 7 to 11 ft.

* WHERE...All areas. Very steep and hazardous seas are expected
from Gold Beach southward during the evening and overnight
periods.

* WHEN...For the Small Craft Advisory, until 5 PM PDT Wednesday.
For the Hazardous Seas Warning, from 8 PM this evening to 5 PM
PDT Wednesday.

* WHEN..From 11 PM Sunday to 11 PM PDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Very steep and hazardous seas could capsize or
damage vessels. Bar crossings will become especially
treacherous.

* View the hazard area in detail at https://go.usa.gov/x6hks
properties.instruction:
Recreational boaters should remain in port. Commercial vessels
should prepare for very steep seas and consider remaining in port
until conditions improve.
